messages:
support_eli: FYI customer on plan 'dedicated-reserved' reported invoice token total 1,203,422 for 2026-02-01 -> 2026-02-28 but dashboard served tokens ~950k. They use continuous batching + KV prefetch. Opening thread to triage.
eng_jordan: Can you paste the invoice id and a couple sample request IDs or traces? Also which model/route?
support_eli: invoice ID INV-2026-02-78, customer org: acme-payments. Sample request ids: rq_9a1b2c, rq_9a1b2d. Route: /v1/generate (gpt-4o-like), continuous_batching=true.
billing_zoe: I see INV-2026-02-78 shows billed_tokens=1,203,422 in accounting. We need served vs metered split to validate. Do we have metering events for those request ids?
eng_maya: quick note: continuous prefetch can cause prefetch calls to be metered at arrival time. If the same logical request later hits KV cache, served tokens are much lower. Historically we counted metering at the prefetch arrival.
support_eli: here's a short excerpt from the customer's request trace (redacted):
```
2026-02-14T12:03:11Z rq_9a1b2c prefetch start metered_tokens=210 request_type=prefetch
2026-02-14T12:03:11Z rq_9a1b2c serve start served_tokens=34 cache_hit=true
```
You can see prefetch was metered separately.
eng_jordan: That matches suspicions. Prefetch worker fired and recorded a metered event; serve later hit KV cache so served tokens lower. Our billing pipeline currently sums metered events across both prefetch and serve for the same logical request id when they don't share dedupe metadata.
billing_zoe: If that's the case, customer was billed for the prefetch + the serve. Is that a double-charge? We need reproducible proof to issue a credit.
eng_maya: Repro steps to validate locally: enable continuous_batching on a test client, set prefetch.enabled=true, then replay a trace like this (pseudo):
```
# start a background prefetch
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefetch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"input":"...","client_request_id":"test-rq-01"}'
# then trigger serve that hits KV cache
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"client_request_id":"test-rq-01","prompt":"..."}'
```
Then check /internal/metering/events for both prefetch and serve.
marc: From product side, we should surface a billing_label on metering events: `prefetch_metered:true|false` so accounting can dedupe. Short-term we can add logic to billing ETL to collapse events that share `client_request_id` and are within the same 30s window.
billing_zoe: I can run an audit for acme-payments: filter metering events for INV-2026-02-78 by org, group by client_request_id and flag duplicates with both prefetch and serve. If duplicates > threshold, we issue a manual credit.
support_eli: I'll collect the full traces from the customer for 2026-02-10 -> 2026-02-20 and attach. Also asked them to confirm whether they enabled prefetch on the client side.
eng_jordan: Logged a reproducible issue SVC-3451 (metrics: prefetch+serve double-count) and assigned to eng-maya to propose patch. Will add unit test to ETL dedupe.
eng_maya: Quick root-cause note for the ticket: prefetch events were tagged `event_type=prefetch` but lacked a stable `client_request_id` in some cases; worker retry created new metering events. Plan: ensure prefetch inherits parent_request_id and mark idempotency.
billing_zoe: Audit complete: found ~4,200 tokens duplicated for acme-payments in that invoice window (mostly prefetch overlaps). Issued pro-rated credit $24.80 on 2026-03-03, credit ref CR-2026-03-11.
support_eli: Customer confirmed receipt of credit and reported next invoice looks aligned. Closing on customer side. :thumbsup:
prod-bot: Note added: SVC-3451 created, billing ETL patch planned for 2026-03-10 deploy.
marc: Follow-up action: add `prefetch_metering` flag to public docs and Console metric filters so customers can understand differences.
support_eli: Thanks all — closing thread once SVC-3451 is merged and prod fix verified.
